Election will determine balance of power in New Caledonia before fresh negotiations with France on the territory’s status Polls opened in the French overseas territory of New Caledonia on Sunday for the archipelago’s first provincial elections since 2019, after the vote was delayed as talks stalled over its political future. The election, initially planned for 2024, will determine the balance of power in New Caledonia ahead of fresh negotiations with France on the territory’s status, with independence remaining the defining political issue. About 192,000 voters will elect 76 councillors for three provincial assemblies – 40 in the South Province, 22 in the North Province and 14 in the Loyalty Islands. Fifty-four of those elected will become members of the Pacific archipelago’s congress, the territory’s main governing institution and the only body authorised to pass local laws.

Members of congress will then elect up to 11 members to the executive branch known as the collegial government. The elections come after the main pro-independence group rejected a deal with France intended to bring stability to the overseas territory. The so-called Bougival Accord would have created a Caledonian state and established a Caledonian nationality enshrined in the French constitution, but would have scrapped any future referendums on independence. Three referendums held in 2018, 2020 and 2021 returned majorities in favour of remaining part of France, although pro-independence groups boycotted the third vote, which was held during the Covid pandemic. But the independence movement retains strong support, particularly among the indigenous Melanesian Kanak population.

Islanders on the French Pacific territory of New Caledonia on Sunday rejected independence in a referendum that revealed weaker-than-expected support for Paris in the resource-rich and strategic outpost. On the final count, 56.4 percent of people rejected the proposition that New Caledonia — some 18,000 kilometres (11,000 miles) from the French mainland — become independent. Turnout was high at 80.63 percent. President Emmanuel Macron expressed his “immense pride that we have taken this historic step together” in an address to the nation, adding it was “a sign of confidence in the French republic, in its future and its values.” The island is home to a quarter of the world’s known supplies of nickel — a vital electronics component — and is a foothold for France in the Pacific where China is gaining influence.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: The Guardian World]
Election will determine balance of power in New Caledonia before fresh negotiations with France on the territory’s status

Polls opened in the French overseas territory of New Caledonia on Sunday for the archipelago’s first provincial elections since 2019, after the vote was delayed as talks stalled over its political future.

The election, initially planned for 2024, will determine the balance of power in New Caledonia ahead of fresh negotiations with France on the territory’s status, with independence remaining the defining political issue.

About 192,000 voters will elect 76 councillors for three provincial assemblies – 40 in the South Province, 22 in the North Province and 14 in the Loyalty Islands.

Fifty-four of those elected will become members of the Pacific archipelago’s congress, the territory’s main governing institution and the only body authorised to pass local laws.

Members of congress will then elect up to 11 members to the executive branch known as the collegial government.

The elections come after the main pro-independence group rejected a deal with France intended to bring stability to the overseas territory.

The so-called Bougival Accord would have created a Caledonian state and established a Caledonian nationality enshrined in the French constitution, but would have scrapped any future referendums on independence.

Three referendums held in 2018, 2020 and 2021 returned majorities in favour of remaining part of France, although pro-independence groups boycotted the third vote, which was held during the Covid pandemic.

But the independence movement retains strong support, particularly among the indigenous Melanesian Kanak population.

A law approved in May added about 10,575 previously excluded “native-born” residents to the electoral roll, including more than 4,000 people with so-called “customary civil status”, which denotes Kanaks.

The change increased the number of eligible voters for Sunday’s poll, after the electoral roll had been frozen under a landmark 1998 agreement.

A previous plan to extend voting rights to thousands of non-Indigenous long-term residents sparked deadly riots in 2024.

The election is taking place under close scrutiny more than two years after the violence, which left 14 people dead and caused more than two billion euros worth of damage.

France has deployed about 2,400 law enforcement officers to New Caledonia, where they will stay until mid-July.

---

[Lähde: Digital Journal]
Islanders on the French Pacific territory of New Caledonia on Sunday rejected independence in a referendum that revealed weaker-than-expected support for Paris in the resource-rich and strategic outpost.

On the final count, 56.4 percent of people rejected the proposition that New Caledonia — some 18,000 kilometres (11,000 miles) from the French mainland — become independent. Turnout was high at 80.63 percent.

President Emmanuel Macron expressed his “immense pride that we have taken this historic step together” in an address to the nation, adding it was “a sign of confidence in the French republic, in its future and its values.”

The island is home to a quarter of the world’s known supplies of nickel — a vital electronics component — and is a foothold for France in the Pacific where China is gaining influence.

But the winning margin in New Caledonia, sometimes referred to in France as “the pebble”, might cause some concern in Paris, as well as in Australia which has been alarmed by Beijing’s designs in the Pacific and its investment in island nations.

payload.title: Uuden-Kaledonian aluevaalit avaavat tien uusiin neuvotteluihin Ranskan kanssa
payload.summary: Uudessa-Kaledoniassa äänestetään ensimmäisissä aluevaaleissa sitten vuoden 2019. Vaalit määrittävät valtasuhteita ennen uusia neuvotteluja alueen asemasta Ranskan yhteydessä.
payload.content:
Uudessa-Kaledoniassa äänestyspaikat avautuivat sunnuntaina ensimmäisissä aluevaaleissa sitten vuoden 2019. Ranskan merentakaisen alueen vaalit oli alun perin määrä järjestää vuonna 2024, mutta niitä lykättiin, kun neuvottelut alueen poliittisesta tulevaisuudesta pysähtyivät. Äänestyksen tulos vaikuttaa valtasuhteisiin ennen uusia keskusteluja Ranskan kanssa, ja itsenäisyys pysyy vaalien keskeisenä poliittisena kysymyksenä.

## Äänestäjät valitsevat maakuntien edustajat

Noin 192 000 äänestäjää valitsee 76 edustajaa kolmeen maakuntakokoukseen. Eteläiseen maakuntaan valitaan 40 edustajaa, pohjoiseen maakuntaan 22 ja Loyalty Islands -saarille 14.

Valituista edustajista 54 nousee Uuden-Kaledonian kongressiin. Kongressi on Tyynenmeren saariston keskeinen hallintoelin ja ainoa elin, jolla on valta säätää paikallisia lakeja. Kongressin jäsenet valitsevat myöhemmin enintään 11 jäsentä toimeenpanevaan elimeen, jota kutsutaan kollegiaaliseksi hallitukseksi.

## Itsenäisyyskysymys jakaa yhä aluetta

Vaalit järjestetään tilanteessa, jossa keskeinen itsenäisyyttä ajava ryhmä on hylännyt Ranskan kanssa laaditun sopimuksen, jonka tarkoituksena oli vakauttaa merentakaisen alueen asemaa. Niin kutsuttu Bougivalin sopimus olisi luonut kaledonialaisen valtion ja kirjannut kaledonialaisen kansalaisuuden Ranskan perustuslakiin. Samalla se olisi kuitenkin poistanut mahdollisuuden tuleviin itsenäisyysäänestyksiin.

Uudessa-Kaledoniassa järjestettiin itsenäisyydestä kansanäänestykset vuosina 2018, 2020 ja 2021. Kaikissa enemmistö kannatti Ranskan yhteydessä pysymistä. Itsenäisyysmieliset ryhmät kuitenkin boikotoivat kolmatta äänestystä, joka järjestettiin koronapandemian aikana.

## Alueella on myös strategista painoa

Itsenäisyysliikkeellä on yhä vahvaa kannatusta etenkin alkuperäiskansaan kuuluvien melanesialaisten kanakien keskuudessa. Aiemmassa kansanäänestyksessä 56,4 prosenttia äänestäjistä vastusti itsenäistymistä, ja äänestysprosentti oli 80,63. Presidentti Emmanuel Macron kuvasi tulosta tuolloin luottamuksen osoitukseksi Ranskan tasavaltaa kohtaan.

Uusi-Kaledonia sijaitsee noin 18 000 kilometrin päässä Ranskan mannermaasta. Alueella on noin neljännes maailman tunnetuista nikkelivaroista, ja se vahvistaa Ranskan asemaa Tyynellämerellä alueella, jossa myös Kiinan vaikutusvalta on kasvanut.

Noin 192 000 äänestäjää valitsee edustajat kolmeen maakuntakokoukseen.
Vaalit vaikuttavat valtasuhteisiin ennen uusia neuvotteluja alueen asemasta Ranskan kanssa.
